message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 250, "amount_cents": 14546}, {"order_id": 251, "amount_cents": 1481}, {"order_id": 255, "amount_cents": 12535}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: I need to verify that the refunds reported by Alpha Co match the refunds recorded in my system before proceeding with payouts.
The refunds reported by Alpha Co match exactly what I have recorded, so there is no discrepancy to address. I can now retrieve the net balances for each customer using net_balance.

The net_balance call failed because '250' is an order ID, not a customer. I need the actual customer identifiers to retrieve their net balances. I will first list all orders to find the corresponding customers.

I have the orders with their customers. Now I can compute the net balance for each customer by subtracting the refunds from the order amounts. I will call net_balance for each customer: acme, birch, cobalt.
I have the net balance for acme (5519 cents). Next I need the net balances for birch and cobalt.
I now have net balances for acme (5519 cents) and birch (13637 cents). I need the net balance for cobalt.
I have the net balances for all customers: acme 5519 cents, birch 13637 cents, cobalt 41289 cents. Now I will record the payouts for each customer.
The payout for acme has been recorded successfully. Next, I will record the payout for birch.

result.error: bad arguments: World.record_payout() got an unexpected keyword argument 'amount_cent'. Did you mean 'amount_cents'?

reply.thought: The previous call failed because the argument name was incorrect; it should be 'amount_cents'. I will correct the spelling and record the payout for birch.
The payout for birch has been recorded successfully. Next, I will record the payout for cobalt.
All payouts have been recorded successfully. I will now summarize the payouts and mark the task as complete.
